responsibilities: Design, build, and maintain semantic models and curated datasets on the Databricks platform, ensuring they are performant, reusable, and aligned with governance standards.
Act as the technical bridge between the central Data Engineering team and transformation/business stakeholders, translating ambiguous business questions into structured data models.
Build and maintain automation/AI-readiness scoring frameworks — turning taxonomy and process data into structured, defensible metrics used in executive business cases.
Produce the quantitative backbone of transformation business cases: current-state baselines, savings and benefit tracking, scenario/what-if models, and before/after comparisons.
Standardise datasets and business logic so that transformation workstreams (cost optimisation, resourcing, margin analysis) build consistently on a shared foundation rather than one-off extracts.
Collaborate with the data engineering team on the design of upstream data assets, ensuring they meet the requirements of scalable, transformation-facing analytics.
Contribute to data assets and pipelines that are structured to support AI, machine learning, and agentic workflows — increasingly the default mode of delivery rather than a side project.
Monitor and optimise the performance of data models and semantic layers, proactively identifying and resolving data quality issues before they reach executive reporting.
Support platform adoption through documentation, standards, and knowledge transfer, contributing to best practices for data modelling, naming conventions, and dataset architecture.
Participate in peer reviews of data models to ensure consistency and quality before release into business-critical decks and workbooks.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Monitor and optimise the performance of data models and semantic layers, proactively identifying and resolving data quality issues before they reach executive reporting
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: The JD repeatedly emphasizes governance standards, data quality, peer reviews, and auditable transformations with no velocity/speed language, clearly rigour.
evidence.domain_risk: Produce the quantitative backbone of transformation business cases... numbers that go straight into executive decks and capital-approval workbooks
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: The role feeds executive/capital-approval decision-making at a global real estate services firm without an explicit financial-reporting or regulatory-compliance override in the JD's own language, a moderate business-decision domain.
evidence.collaboration_width: central Data Engineering team; transformation/business stakeholders
evidence.data_team_maturity: Our lakehouse platform is mature and well established. It is built on Databricks and already runs the business end to end
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: The JD explicitly states the lakehouse platform is mature and well established, running the entire business end-to-end, an unambiguous mature classification.
evidence.jd_authorship: Build and maintain automation/AI-readiness scoring frameworks — turning taxonomy and process data into structured, defensible metrics used in executive business cases
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities name precise deliverables (AI-readiness scoring, business-case baselines, scenario models) and specific tools (Databricks, DAX, Power BI) with exceptional specificity, giving a very clear picture of daily work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: You will sit between data engineering and the business. That means turning commercial questions into semantic models... that leaders across EMEA and APAC rely on
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role explicitly bridges data engineering and business/commercial stakeholders (cost optimisation, resourcing, margin analysis) with genuinely equal weight, so mixed.
evidence.autonomy_level: You will take on problems nobody has written the playbook for, make calls that matter, and build depth across several domains early enough to shape where the platform goes next
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The JD explicitly frames the role around making impactful decisions and shaping platform direction on unprecedented problems, an unambiguously strategic framing.
evidence.ai_role: getting them ready for agentic and AI-led delivery... Contribute to data assets and pipelines that are structured to support AI, machine learning, and agentic workflows — increasingly the default mode of delivery rather than a side project
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate is explicitly expected to build data infrastructure and AI-readiness scoring frameworks that AI/agentic systems consume, a clear and heavily emphasized AI-enabler responsibility.
evidence.testing_framing: Participate in peer reviews of data models to ensure consistency and quality before release into business-critical decks and workbooks
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Peer review and quality assurance are explicitly framed as an owned responsibility before release, not just a listed skill.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: proactively identifying and resolving data quality issues before they reach executive reporting
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: There is a clear concern about data quality reaching executive decision-makers, but it is secondary to the transformation/AI-capability-building framing rather than a dominant compliance register, so moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Our lakehouse platform is mature and well established... What comes next is the harder part, putting agentic capability to work at real enterprise scale
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The role both operates on an existing mature lakehouse platform (fix/scale) and pioneers new agentic AI capability that nobody in the sector has built yet (greenfield), a genuine and explicit mix.
evidence.language_gate: Fluent in English; additional European languages an advantage.
